title: Ephemeral steward checkpoints and re-eval playbook for prompt corpus
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Config and model variant changes frequently trigger large-scale re-evals against canonical prompt corpora. Current flows require manual curator intervention, long lock windows, and central ownership which creates bottlenecks for fast rollouts and increases time-to-detect regressions.

Goal: Define a lightweight, auditable ‘ephemeral steward’ checkpoint workflow and an automated re-eval playbook that allows scoped promptset snapshots, temporary custodial ACLs, and deterministic re-eval runs tied to specific config/model diffs. The workflow should minimize curator interruption while preserving lineage, signatures, and rollback capability.

Scope: Prompt corpus snapshotting, ephemeral ACL issuance, signed attestations for checkpoints, CI-orchestrated re-eval job templates, and an operator playbook for human-in-the-loop edge cases. Does not include UI rollout in Console for now (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Can create an immutable promptset snapshot (signed hash + manifest) from a workspace without requiring full steward rotation
Ephemeral ACL tokens can be minted with scoped permissions (read-only for specific snapshot GUIDs) and TTLs <= 72 hours
Re-eval CI job template consumes snapshot manifest and produces per-metric baselines and regression artifacts stored in S3 with standardized metadata
Automated gating rule can mark a config/model change as requiring human review if regression >= delta thresholds for top-3 metrics
All snapshot and ACL actions are audited and queryable via the audit-log service and linked to the originating config diff (git SHA or runtime-config ID)
plan: Design manifest schema: snapshot GUID, prompt IDs, source refs, signer, provenance signature, and checksum per-example
Implement snapshot API endpoint (internal-only) that atomically pins a promptset and emits signed manifest (use KMS signing)
Build ephemeral ACL service/harness to mint short-lived tokens scoped to snapshot GUIDs; integrate with existing RBAC service
Create CI re-eval job template (Docker + orchestration) that accepts manifest URL and produces artifacts (scores, diffs, example counterexamples)
Wire gating: add webhooks from config-change service to enqueue re-eval jobs; implement simple threshold-based classifier to surface candidate regressions
Create operator playbook with steps for triage, rebase, re-run, and rollback (stored in Confluence and linked in ticket)
End-to-end smoke tests and a staged rollout on the 'staging-evals' cluster before enabling on prod
rollout_steps: v0: internal rollout to research and one stewarding team (manual snapshot + manual ACL request)
v1: enable snapshot API + ephemeral ACL for all steward teams; CI template available; keep manual gating
v2: enable automated enqueue from config-change webhooks with opt-in gating for low-risk changes
v3: full opt-out for automated gating and Console integration (separate PM ticket)
regressions_detection_playbook: On regression alert, collect the snapshot manifest, model/config diff, and re-eval job logs
Run focused re-evals on top-k failing examples with higher sampling to reduce noise
If regression confirmed, create rollback job that pins traffic to previous model variant or config until remediation
Notify stakeholders (stewards, PM, SRE) with an incident summary and attach artifacts
Postmortem and dataset remediation plan: add failing examples to 'investigation' bucket and flag for curation
